title: AI Engineering OS project configuration
description: Contents of .ai-engineering/project.yaml (or project.json). Declares the human-approved technology, process and safety envelope for one project. The AI Engineering OS is technology-neutral: everything technology-specific is declared here, never in the plugin.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file targets.

key.description: Short uppercase prefix for traceability identifiers, e.g. SFTP -> SFTP-REQ-001.

tier.description: 1 = business critical, 4 = experimental. Drives default risk posture.

compliance.description: Regimes the project is subject to, e.g. PCI-DSS, GDPR, SOC2.

technology.description: The approved stack. Any technology not listed here requires a technology decision (AP-03) before use. Every field is optional because not every project has every layer.

api_style.description: e.g. rest, graphql, grpc, event-driven, sftp-protocol.

edition.description: Declares which GitLab features may be assumed. Core workflows must work on ce.

production.description: True marks the environment as production: agents may never mutate it without human approval.

data.description: Environments carrying production data inherit production-grade access rules.

platform.description: e.g. kubernetes, ecs, vm-systemd, serverless, on-premise-appliance.

rollback.description: How a release is reverted, in one sentence.

environments.description: The promotion ladder, in order, ending at production. Promotion follows this list and cannot skip a rung. Empty means the project does not promote through environments, which is a legitimate answer for a library or a tool.

differs_from_next.description: What this environment does NOT tell you about the next one. This is the field worth arguing over: 'it worked in staging' is only evidence to the extent staging resembles production, and the difference is what decides how much.

requirements.description: Project-specific security requirements stated as testable obligations.

secret_management.description: Where secrets live. Never the repository.

threat_model.description: Path to the current threat model artifact.

knowledge.description: Where project artifacts live. Defaults follow docs/knowledge-structure.md.

language_intelligence.description: How this project gives Claude Code language intelligence: go-to-definition, find-references, hover types and diagnostics from a language server. Claude Code reads language-server configuration ONLY from a plugin's own .lsp.json (or a plugin.json lspServers field); it never reads this file. So this section is the human-approved record of what the project expects, and the companion plugin named in 'plugin' is what actually delivers it. Declaring a server here does not start one. See docs/lsp.md.

provider.description: 'companion-plugin': a separate plugin, owned by this project or the organization, carries the .lsp.json. 'none': the project has decided to work without a language server, and agents fall back to grep and reading files. 'none' is a legitimate answer; an absent section is an undeclared one.

plugin.description: The plugin@marketplace identifier of the companion plugin whose .lsp.json carries these servers. Required in practice when provider is companion-plugin: without it nobody can tell which plugin to install.

servers.description: The servers that companion plugin declares, mirrored here so the approved toolchain is reviewable in one place. Keep in step with the companion plugin's .lsp.json; nothing enforces the match at runtime.

name.description: The key this server appears under in the companion plugin's .lsp.json.

command.description: The language-server executable. Claude Code rejects a command containing a space unless it is an absolute path; arguments belong in 'args'. The binary is NOT installed by the plugin: it must already be on PATH.

extensions.description: File extensions this server answers for, each leading with a dot. These become the .lsp.json extensionToLanguage keys. Two plugins claiming the same extension is a conflict Claude Code reports and resolves by first registration, so keep them disjoint from any other LSP plugin installed.

language.description: LSP language id these extensions map to, e.g. 'go', 'python'. Defaults to the server name.

install.description: How a developer or a CI image obtains the binary. Recorded because a missing binary shows up only as 'Executable not found in $PATH' in the /plugin Errors tab, which is easy to miss and easy to fix.

diagnostics.description: Whether the server's diagnostics are pushed into the agent's context after edits. Defaults to true in Claude Code. Set false to keep navigation but stop a noisy linter spending context.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs to know, e.g. why a layer has no server.

open_decisions.description: Decisions the project knows it has not made yet. Agents must treat these as blocking rather than guessing.

extensions.description: Free-form project-specific configuration. Never read by the plugin; available to project-local skills.

ai.description: Project-level AI Engineering OS overrides. A project may tighten freely; it may not lower a role below the model floor for its risk class.

model_overrides.description: Per-role model and effort overrides. Resolved by scripts/resolve_model.py, which refuses any value below the risk floor.

execution_overrides.description: Per-stage execution overrides, e.g. forcing 'inline' where agent teams are unavailable.

agent_teams_available.description: False where the organization has not enabled the experimental agent-teams feature. Stages declaring 'team' fall back to 'subagent'.

available_models.description: The models this Claude organization permits. Empty means unrestricted. When an organization's allowlist excludes the model a risk floor requires, HIGH and CRITICAL work blocks instead of running on a weaker one: a floor that silently degrades is not a floor, and the resolver used to keep reporting the model it wanted while the work ran below it.

approval.description: Named humans who hold each approval authority in this project. An approval category with no named human cannot be satisfied.

ai_system.description: What this project's own software uses a model for. Distinct from `ai`, which is about how the AI Engineering OS runs this project's roles -- two different subjects that share a word. Without this section a project had no way to say that the thing it builds is an AI system, so the AI engineering skills had nothing to trigger on and a model provider was a technology decision with nowhere to be recorded. Absent means the project builds no AI features; it is never inferred.

builds_ai_features.description: A human decision, like every other entry in this file. Observing a model call in the repository is not a declaration.

capabilities.description: Which model-backed capabilities the product actually uses. Each one brings its own failure modes and its own evaluation.

model_providers.description: Approved model providers and versions. A technology decision under AP-03 like any other, and pinned: an unpinned version changes the system's behaviour without a deployment and invalidates every evaluation that passed.

autonomy.description: The blast radius of a wrong answer, and the axis that decides how much of the rest matters. irreversible-action needs a named human in the loop and the approval its stage carries.

evaluation.description: Where the evaluation dataset lives and what the current baseline is. An AI component with no dataset has no definition of done anybody can check.

dataset.description: Path or identifier of the evaluation dataset.

baseline.description: The production configuration a candidate is compared against: prompt, model, index and dataset versions.

thresholds.description: Gates on the comparison rather than on an absolute, so they survive a dataset getting harder.

data_in_prompts.description: What project data may be sent to a provider, and what the provider retains. A data-classification decision, recorded before it is implemented rather than discovered afterwards.

adr.description: Identifier of the ADR that approved this choice.

identity.description: Stable identity, e.g. a GitLab username or group.
